args.text: [lane-stoat] Three risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System) answers for too long: (1) Stale answers: users are sent to an old address after a server moves, causing outages. (2) Slow recovery: a fix or failover takes ages to reach users because old records linger. (3) Prolonged harm from bad data: if a false answer is cached, it stays in use for longer.

[lane-stoat] Idempotent retries matter because networks fail unpredictably, so a client often cannot tell whether its first request worked, and it must be able to try again. If the request is idempotent (repeating it gives the same result as doing it once), a retry cannot cause harm such as charging a customer twice.

[lane-stoat] Two trade-offs of UUIDv7 (a 128-bit identifier that starts with a timestamp) as a primary key: (1) Because the first part is a timestamp, the ID reveals roughly when a row was created, which may leak information. (2) It is 16 bytes, larger than a 4 or 8 byte integer, so indexes use more space, though it is far kinder to index ordering than fully random UUIDs.

[lane-stoat] A write-ahead log (a file where a database records each change before applying it to the main data) lets the system recover after a crash by replaying or undoing those recorded changes. It also makes writes faster and safer, because appending to a log is cheap and the main data files can be updated later.

[lane-stoat] (1) Pinning the client version keeps results comparable: if the client changes between runs, a speed difference might come from the client rather than the system being tested. (2) It makes the benchmark repeatable, so anyone can rerun it later and get the same setup, without hidden changes to defaults or behaviour.

[lane-stoat] Backpressure is a signal from a busy consumer telling producers to slow down or wait, so a queue does not fill up without limit. It protects the system by trading a little delay or refused work for stability, rather than running out of memory or crashing.

[lane-stoat] Two ways a cron job can run twice: (1) the same job is installed on two servers, or in two places on one server; (2) a slow run is still going when the next scheduled run starts. One guard: take a lock before starting, such as a lock file or a database lock, and exit at once if another run holds it.

[lane-stoat] A tombstone is a marker saved in place of deleted data, to record that the item was removed. Without it, a copy that missed the deletion could send the old value back to the other copies and bring it back to life. Tombstones are cleared away after a set period, once all copies are expected to have seen them.

[lane-stoat] Two signs that a test is flaky rather than failing: (1) it passes and fails on the same code with no change between runs. (2) The result depends on things like timing, run order or shared data, so a re-run often gives a different answer. A truly failing test fails every time.

[lane-stoat] A lease-based lock gives a client the lock for a set time, and each side judges that time using its own clock. If the clocks drift apart (clock skew), the lock server may think the lease has ended while the client thinks it still holds it. A second client can then be given the lock, so two clients act at once and the lock no longer protects the shared data.
